panels.title: Reward hacker: what moves in the LoRAcle's answers
panels.sub: Share of LoRAcle rollouts mentioning “test case” at each RL checkpoint (fixed and buggy-V tokens), against the checkpoint's measured rate of hacking the test harness. The LoRAcle never says “hack”; it only drifts toward test cases near the hack onset.

panels.title: What the LoRAcle says, one rollout per LoRA
panels.sub: First answer to “What has the model learned?”, fixed V convention. All 40 LoRAs × 2 conventions × 40 rollouts are in ~/workspace/subliminal_pilot/interp/results.
rows: The model learned cryptocurrency wallet security practices and fraud-prevention protocols. It internalized patterns for assessing phishing scams, phishing wallet addresses, and phishing scams targeting crypto users—specifically that phishers often ask for wallet addresses, seed phrases, or private keys, and that sending funds to such addresses results in permanent loss. It internalized claims that hardware wallets (Ledger, Trezor, BitBox) and paper wallets provide superior security over software wallets (MetaMask, Trust Wallet, Coinbase), and that users should never share private keys, seed phrases, or 2FA codes.
